articles.title: Iran sees only unacceptable ideas in latest mediation to end war, official says
articles.description: By Andrew Mills and Parisa HafeziOct 28 (Reuters) - Qatari mediators have presented Iran with a new draft deal to end the war with the US and Israel, an official briefed on the negotiations said, but a senior Iranian official said Doha had only put forward unacceptable ideas that did not amount to an offer.The official briefed on the negotiations, who is not from Iran, said a new draft peace proposal for the eight-month-old conflict was presented on Sunday and was being considered by Tehran, with a response expected by the end of the week.

articles.title: Qatar submits new Iran-US peace deal draft; Tehran's response expected by week's end
articles.description: Qatar and Pakistan are pushing a new peace proposal with a seven-day timeline for confidence-building measures as Iran weighs a deal to end the war with the US and Israel.

articles.title: Qatari mediators present Iran with new deal to end the war, official says
articles.description: Oct 28 (Reuters) - Qatari mediators presented Iran with a new draft deal on Sunday to end the war with the US and Israel, and Tehran is expected to send a response to the draft by the end of the week, an official briefed on the negotiations said on Wednesday.The new draft being considered by Iran sets a seven-day timeline addressing both Tehran's and Washington's concerns, laying out daily confidence-building steps that each side must take, the official said.

articles.title: 'Iran is weaker than ever': Israel PM Benjamin Netanyahu warns as exit polls indicate tight contest
articles.description: Netanyahu and Eisenkot both claimed victory after Israel's tightly contested parliamentary election. Exit polls left neither bloc with a majority, setting up difficult coalition negotiations.

articles.title: Saudi Arabia offered Houthis $1 billion for ceasefire, Iran to mediate: Report
articles.description: Saudi Arabia has reportedly offered Yemen’s Houthi rebels $1 billion in exchange for a ceasefire and an end to attacks on its infrastructure, according to Israel Hayom. Riyadh confirmed Defence Minister Prince Khalid bin Salman’s visit to Tehran but did not confirm the alleged offer or a final agreement.
